items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the white knight on e6 attacks (a square holding a piece counts).

claims.statement: The knight on e6 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: A knight moves in an L: two squares one way and one the other.
From e6 go two squares sideways or two up and down, then one at right angles.
Eight squares in all: c5, c7, d4, d8, f4, f8, g5 and g7.
items.explain: A knight on e6 reaches c5, c7, d4, d8, f4, f8, g5 and g7. Two of them hold Black pieces: the queen on d8 and the bishop on f8. That is the fork.

items.prompt: Black's queen could go to any of these squares: a5, b6, c7, c8, d4, d5, d6, d7 (all legal). Tap those where the knight on e6 could capture her at once.

claims.statement: The queen on d8 can move to exactly these squares (and e8 is occupied by the king).
The knight on e6 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: Use the list of squares the knight attacks.
Compare it with the queen's destinations.
Two destinations are also on the knight's list: c7 and d4.
items.explain: The knight attacks c7 and d4, and both are on the queen's list. A queen that lands on c7 or d4 is simply captured. The other queen squares are not attacked by the knight, but, as the next boards show, other things go wrong.

items.prompt: White to move after 7...Qd7. Find a strong move (two moves are close; the second is slightly weaker).

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 8.Nxf8 and 8.Nc5 are both within 60 cp of the top choice.
After 8.Nc5 the knight attacks the queen on d7.
Engine, depth 16: 8.Nxg7+ is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The knight on e6 attacks the bishop on f8.
Check which captures are safe for the knight.
Taking on f8 is safe: the king recaptures but White gets a follow-up.
items.explain: The bishop on f8 is defended only by the king, so the capture is a trade of knight for bishop, and the next knight jump forks queen and bishop. The knight can also hop to c5 and attack the queen at once. Engine, depth 16: both keep White clearly ahead.

feedback_by_move.e6g7: Nxg7+ loses the knight for a pawn: the bishop takes it. The engine rates it at least 400 cp worse.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Ne5 (queen on d7). Is the black queen attacked by the knight on e5?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks d7.

hints: Work out the knight's squares from e5.
A knight on e5 reaches d7, f7, c6, g6, c4, g4, d3 and f3.
d7 is on the list.
items.explain: A knight on e5 attacks d7, f7, c6, g6, c4, g4, d3 and f3. The queen stands on d7, so she is attacked, and so is the bishop on g6.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Ne5 (queen on d6). Is the black queen attacked by the knight on e5?

claims.statement: No white piece attacks d6.

hints: Work out the knight's squares from e5.
d6 is next to e5 but not on the knight's list.
Knights never attack the square next to them on a rank, file or diagonal.
items.explain: The knight on e5 does not attack d6 (a knight never attacks a neighbouring square). Only the bishop on g6 is attacked. This is the one difference between the two refusals: queen on d7 is forked, queen on d6 is not.

items.prompt: White to move after 7...Qb6. The bishop on f8 hangs, but a quieter move is stronger. Find it.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 8.Ne5 is the best move.
Engine, depth 16: 8.Nxf8 is at least 250 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The knight on f3 can move without capturing anything.
Look for a square from which it attacks a piece and prepares a second attack.
The knight goes to e5: it attacks the bishop on g6 and can go to c4 next.
items.explain: The knight on e5 attacks the bishop on g6 and threatens to go to c4, attacking the queen. Black cannot meet both threats, and the knight on e6 is still there. Engine, depth 16: White is far ahead.

feedback_by_move.e6f8: Taking the bishop wins nothing by force: Black recaptures and the engine rates this at least 250 cp worse than the quiet knight move.

items.prompt: White to move after 7...Qd5. Find the move that wins the queen.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 8.Nc7+ is the best move.
Nc7+ wins at least 5 points of material.

hints: A knight check can also attack another piece.
Which squares does a knight on c7 attack?
A knight on c7 attacks e8 and d5 (and a8, a6, b5, e6).
items.explain: From c7 the knight gives check to the king on e8 and attacks the queen on d5. The king must move, and the knight takes the queen.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Ne5. The bishop on g6 is attacked. Find a retreat. All three retreats keep the bishop, but Black is worse.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Bh7, ...Be4 and ...Bf5 are all within 40 cp of the top choice.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is at least 80 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: White is clearly ahead here (at least 100 cp).

hints: The bishop is attacked by a knight and defended only by the f7 pawn.
Retreat along the diagonal or trade on your own terms.
Any of h7, e4 or f5 keeps the bishop.
items.explain: The bishop can step back along its diagonal to h7, e4 or f5. Ignoring the attack lets White take on g6 and wreck Black's pawns. Engine, depth 16: the three retreats are within 40 cp of each other, and White is clearly ahead after each; this is what the refusal costs.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: Develops but allows Nxg6+ and ...fxg6, which wrecks the pawn structure. The engine rates it at least 80 cp worse.

items.prompt: Black to move after 7...fxe6 8.Ne5. According to the engine at depth 16, who is better?

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: Black is ahead here (White's side at most -50 cp).

hints: Count the pieces first.
Black has taken a whole knight.
The engine rates Black as clearly better.
items.explain: Black is a knight up and White has only some development to show. Engine, depth 16: Black is ahead by more than half a pawn, even though White has the initiative.

items.prompt: Black to move after 7...Qd6 8.Nxf8 Kxf8 9.Be2. According to the engine at depth 16, who is better?

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: White is ahead here (at least 80 cp).

hints: Count the pieces first.
The pieces are level.
Black's king has lost castling and White is ahead in development.
items.explain: The pieces are level, but Black's king cannot castle and White has more pieces out. Engine, depth 16: White is better. This is the price of the best refusal.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...b5. Don't save the bishop: find the move that wins at least a piece.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 10.Bxe6 is the best move.
Engine, depth 16: 10.Bxb5 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The bishop on c4 is attacked, but you may have something better than saving it.
Which pawn does the bishop attack in the other direction?
Take the e6 pawn: it opens lines to f7.
items.explain: Taking e6 attacks the bishop on f7, which guards h5 and e6, and the knight on e5 also attacks f7. If Black recaptures, the queen comes to h5 with a forced mate. Engine, depth 16: White is clearly winning.

feedback_by_move.c4b5: Taking the pawn wins a pawn but gives Black time: the engine rates it at least 400 cp worse than Bxe6.

items.prompt: White to move after 10...Bxe6. Find the forced mate.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 11.Qh5+ is the best move.
11.Qh5+ mates in three.

hints: The black king has few squares and the bishop on f7 has left.
A check along the h5-e8 diagonal is available.
Qh5+ and then Qxg6+ and Qxf7#; the other block loses at once.
items.explain: The queen checks from h5 and the bishop that used to guard that diagonal has gone to e6. Black has two blocks. After ...g6 the queen takes with check, Black interposes the bishop and the queen takes it: mate in three. After ...Bf7 the queen mates at once.

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...fxe6 is the best move.

hints: The knight attacks two of your pieces.
Taking the knight removes the problem.
The f7 pawn captures on e6.
items.explain: Black takes the knight and is a piece up; every refusal loses castling, time, or more.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the knight move that attacks two black pieces at once.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 9.Ne5 is the best move.

hints: A knight jump can attack two pieces at once.
Which squares does the knight on f3 reach?
e5 attacks the queen and the bishop.
items.explain: The knight on e5 attacks the queen on d7 and the bishop on g6. The queen moves and the bishop falls.

items.prompt: White to move. The knight on e6 is attacked, and the black queen is on b6. Find the move that wins material.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 9.Nc4 is the best move.

hints: The queen is on b6 and your knight can attack it.
Which knight move attacks b6?
A knight on c4 attacks b6.
items.explain: The knight on c4 attacks the queen on b6. Black can take the knight on e6, but the queen is lost afterwards.

items.prompt: White to move after 7...Qa5+ 8.Bd2 Qb6. Find the quiet knight move with two threats.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 9.Ne5 is the best move.

hints: The bishop on f8 hangs, but a quieter move is stronger.
Which knight move attacks the bishop on g6 and prepares an attack on the queen?
The knight goes to e5.
items.explain: The quiet knight move to e5 attacks the bishop on g6 and threatens Nc4 against the queen, the same idea as after 7...Qb6. Engine, depth 16: White is far ahead.
